title: How to Get Teams and Frontline Managers to Actually Use a Feedback Analytics Platform After Launch
summary: Measure the first decision made outside the insights team, not go-live. Then add traceability, scoped manager slices, and scheduled digests.
body_markdown:
The contract is signed, the data is flowing, and the dashboards look good in the kickoff deck. Three months later, the insights team is still the only group logging in. Store managers get a monthly PDF they don't open. Regional leads ask an analyst for "a quick cut" of the same numbers the platform already shows them. This is a common way for a feedback analytics rollout to fail. It rarely shows up in a go-live report.


The fix is to stop measuring launch and start measuring use. A feedback analytics platform is adopted when someone outside the insights team makes a decision from it without being chased. Getting there takes three moves. Make every number traceable to the comments behind it. Give each store, branch, or station manager their own scoped slice. Push scheduled reports to the people who will never log in. Thematic supports all three: themes trace back to verbatims, permissions scope to individual dashboards, and email digests deliver each manager's view on a schedule.


Below is a five-step process for driving adoption after launch, a worked example from Community Health System, and a diagnostic table for figuring out why a rollout has stalled.


## The 5-step process


1. **Redefine "done" as the first decision made outside the insights team.** Track decisions, not logins.
2. **Make every number traceable to the verbatims behind it.** People act on what they can check.
3. **Give each frontline manager their own scoped slice.** A store manager needs their store, not the company.
4. **Push scheduled reports to people who never log in.** Meet non-users in their inbox.
5. **Diagnose the stall by symptom, not by retraining everyone.** Each failure pattern has a specific cause.


## Step 1: Redefine "done" as the first decision made outside the insights team


Most rollouts are declared finished at go-live: sources connected, themes built, dashboards published. That's configuration. Adoption is the point where teams outside the insights function use the platform unprompted.


The ceiling is low. According to a[BARC and Eckerson Group study](https://barc.com/news/new-study-identifies-drivers-of-bi-and-analytics-adoption-in-companies-today/) of 214 data and analytics leaders, only 25% of employees actively use business intelligence (BI) and analytics tools on average, "reflecting minimal growth in the past seven years." A feedback platform inherits that ceiling unless you plan around it.


How to do it:


- **Name the first decision before launch.** For example: "the operations lead reprioritizes store maintenance using the top negative theme."
- **Name the decision owner.** One person outside insights, with a date.
- **Log decisions, not sessions.** Date, person, theme, action. A spreadsheet is enough.


**Common mistake:** reporting weekly active users as the success metric. A manager can log in weekly and never change anything.


## Step 2: Make every number traceable to the verbatims behind it


Frontline managers distrust numbers they didn't produce. If a dashboard says "wait times" drove a score drop, the first question is "which customers said that?" If the answer is "trust the model," adoption stalls.


Traceability is what converts a chart into something a manager will defend in a meeting. In Thematic, "you can see exactly which customer comments were grouped into each theme and why," as the[auditable AI article](https://getthematic.com/insights/auditable-transparent-ai-feedback-analytics) puts it. Dashboard widgets let users click a theme to see example comments inline.


How to do it:


- **Open every review meeting on a verbatim, not a chart.** Read two or three comments aloud before showing the number.
- **Test the click path.** Ask a manager to go from their score to the comments behind it, unaided, in under a minute.
- **Fix themes the frontline disputes.** If a manager says a theme lumps two problems together, split it. Visible corrections build trust.


[Mitre 10](https://getthematic.com/insights/humanising-hardware-how-mitre10-made-voice-of-customer-actionable-with-thematic) , the New Zealand hardware cooperative, shows what this looks like in practice. Its agile development team brings customer feedback into planning sessions, "drilling down to read individual verbatim comments to understand pain points at a human level."


## Step 3: Give each frontline manager their own scoped slice


A company-wide dashboard is useful to the insights team and nearly useless to a store manager. The manager's question is always local: what are customers saying about my location this week?


Thematic permissions are[scoped to individual datasets and dashboards](https://getthematic.com/insights/control-who-sees-customer-feedback) rather than the whole account, with four default roles (Dataset Admin, User Admin, Analyst, and Viewer). That lets you build one dashboard per region, branch, or station, filter it to that unit, and grant each manager access to their own.


How to do it:


- **Build the slice around the manager's unit of control.** Store, branch, station, or team, whichever they can actually change.
- **Limit each slice to a few widgets.** Score, top themes, what changed, and a link to comments.
- **Grant Viewer access by default.** Most frontline managers need to read, not configure. It's worth checking[whether every viewer needs a paid seat](https://getthematic.com/insights/per-seat-licensing-feedback-insights) before you size the rollout.


Once each manager has a slice, the next question is how their unit compares with the rest. For that layer, see[how to benchmark customer experience (CX) across store locations](https://getthematic.com/insights/benchmark-cx-across-locations) .


## Step 4: Push scheduled reports to people who never log in


Some managers will never open a new tool. That isn't a training failure. It's a delivery problem.


Thematic can send dashboards as scheduled email reports from the dashboard's Share button, as the[Sharing Dashboards help article](https://help.getthematic.com/article/182-sharing-dashboards) explains. Dashboard filters carry through to the email, so each manager receives their own slice. Scheduled sends work when new data loads to the dataset on a regular cadence. Anyone can receive the email, but recipients need a Thematic account to open the linked dashboard, so set up accounts for the managers you expect to click through.


How to do it:


- **Match the schedule to decision rhythm.** Store operations need a shorter cycle than regional planning.
- **Subscribe managers yourself.** Waiting for people to opt in to a new report puts the burden on the least engaged. Send it by default and adjust if someone asks to stop.
- **Watch for replies.** A manager who replies to a digest with a question is adopting, even if they never log in.


The digest is the on-ramp, and the scoped dashboard is where a curious manager lands. For the reporting mechanics, see[how to automate customer feedback reporting](https://getthematic.com/insights/automate-customer-feedback-reporting) .


## Step 5: Diagnose the stall by symptom, not by retraining everyone


When usage flattens, the default response is another round of training. Training fixes a skills gap. Most stalls aren't.


**Symptom** **Likely cause** **Fix**


Managers ask analysts for cuts the dashboard already shows The slice isn't scoped to their unit Build a filtered dashboard per unit (Step 3)


Numbers get challenged in meetings, then ignored No path from score to comments Lead with verbatims; test the click path (Step 2)


Digests go out, nothing changes No named decision or owner Assign the first decision and log it (Step 1)


High logins, no decisions Dashboard answers the insights team's questions, not the manager's Rebuild widgets around local, controllable themes


Usage spikes after launch, then drops The data went stale or the cadence doesn't match Check that data loads on schedule; align digest cadence


Diagnose one region or team at a time. Start by asking one manager who stopped using it why.


## A worked example: Community Health System


Community Health System is a not-for-profit healthcare network serving California's central San Joaquin Valley. Its Organizational Development team needed to get feedback results to 250 departments, at roughly an hour of preparation per department. Alexandra Clifton, Organizational Development Partner, described the old approach: "Before, we were doing everything in an Excel spreadsheet and just generating information and having conversations with people in real time."


The change was structural.[According to the case study](https://getthematic.com/insights/community-health-systems-actionable-insights) , the team uses Thematic to produce 250 one-page department reports in three days. The result: 100% of directors have access to standardized feedback reports, a formal deliverable instead of an ad-hoc conversation or a spreadsheet.


Three of the five steps show up here. Each department gets its own scoped slice (Step 3). The reports carry comment-based insights, not only scores, which is traceability (Step 2). And the insights reach directors without them having to ask for a meeting, the same principle as Step 4. As Clifton put it: "We can officially finally say that there's a deliverable with comments that says everyone had access to these three things with comments, director and above, which has never existed before."


## Common mistakes to avoid


- **Declaring success at go-live.** Go-live is configuration. Measure the first decision made outside the insights team.
- **Treating low logins as a training problem.** Most stalls are scoping, trust, or delivery problems. Diagnose first. If a genuine skills gap remains, see[role-based voice of the customer training](https://getthematic.com/insights/voice-of-the-customer-training) .
- **Giving everyone the same company-wide dashboard.** Scope each view to the unit the manager controls.
- **Hiding the comments behind the charts.** If a manager can't reach the verbatims in one click, they won't trust the number.
- **Waiting for people to log in.** Subscribe them to digests of their own slice.
- **Rolling out to every team at once.** Start with one region, log one decision, then expand.


## The short answer


To get teams and frontline managers to actually use a feedback analytics platform after launch, measure the first decision made outside the insights team rather than the go-live date. Then remove the three blockers that stall most rollouts: numbers people can't verify, dashboards that aren't about their location, and tools they'll never open. With Thematic, that means themes that trace back to verbatims, dashboards scoped to each store, branch, or station, and email digests that deliver each manager's slice on a schedule.


If you're still evaluating platforms, see[how to get buy-in before you buy](https://getthematic.com/insights/get-buy-in-customer-feedback-platform) , which covers the earlier stages.
